declared.how: a daily figure published by the provider in tokens

derived.how: a published request cap x 500 tokens a reply, or a published unit price divided into a published allowance; the arithmetic is in each row's volume_evidence

drawn.how: tokens_per_hour_drawn x 24 from data/drawn.jsonl: extrapolated from a 60-minute draw, used only where nothing above exists

aihubmix.evidence: The generous number costs one dollar. A new account gets 10 trial calls and nothing else; a single top-up of $1 switches the account permanently to daily quotas. So the 1,000,000 tokens a day is real, recurring and unlimited in time - but it is not free until you have paid a dollar once, and this row says so rather than printing the big number on its own. 100 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 50,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Requests per day, at 100, long before the million tokens. Applies per ACCOUNT.

cerebras.evidence: Their pricing page on 2026-09-06 describes free access only as 'Free Trial: $5 in free credits after making an account' and publishes no daily free-tier ceiling at all. The numbers below are what the response headers of a free-trial key reported between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-07. They may be trial allowance rather than a standing free tier. Re-measure before relying on them. 1,000,000 tokens/day is the provider's own token figure (MEASURED). Binding limit: 5 requests per minute. Two calls inside the same minute need roughly 13 s between them. Applies per ACCOUNT.

cloudflare.evidence: Cloudflare bills in Neurons, not tokens, and publishes both the free allocation and the conversion on the same page. 10,000 Neurons a day divided by 34,868 Neurons per million output tokens is about 286,795 output tokens a day on llama-3.1-8b: their two numbers, our division, so it is marked DERIVED and never counted as measured. Where the tracked model's own Neuron price is in `neuron_cost_examples`, rank.py derives that model's figure from it instead; llama-3.3-70b costs six times more per output token than the 8b model. Seven models are excluded from the free tier entirely and need a paid billing method. 10,000 Neurons/day / 34,868 Neurons per 1M output tokens, @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8-fast. This model's own unit price is not on file, so the figure is the provider-level one and this model's real allowance may be lower. Binding limit: Neurons per day, at 10,000. On a small text model that is roughly a quarter of a million output tokens; on a large one, far fewer. Applies per ACCOUNT.

google.evidence: The public docs page no longer prints the per-model table; it points you at aistudio.google.com/rate-limit, which needs a login. The figures below were read off that console screen on 2026-09-06. Free tier means literally 'no billing account linked': linking one moves the project to Tier 1 and off these numbers. Because the limits are per PROJECT, a second API key in the same project buys you nothing. 500 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 250,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Requests per DAY on the Flash models. 20/day is a handful of conversations, not a workload. Applies per PROJECT.

hetzner.evidence: 232,551 tokens drawn per hour x 24: extrapolated from a 60-minute draw on 2026-09-07

kenari.evidence: Three tiers by account status. A new account is Solo: 50 free-model requests a day and 5 a minute. A top-up of Rp 10,000 moves it to Payer, at 1,000 a day. The header measured on 2026-09-07 read x-ratelimit-limit 5, which matches the Solo per-minute figure. 50 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 25,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Fifty free requests a day until a top-up moves the account to Payer. Applies per ACCOUNT.

openrouter.evidence: The daily cap depends on lifetime credits purchased, and applies across ALL :free models combined, not per model. This condition is the one most lists drop, which makes their number wrong for a new account by a factor of twenty. What a NEW account gets; rises to 1,000/day under the conditions in LIMITS.md, and is shared across all free models. 50 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 25,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. rpd is tiered by lifetime credits purchased: see free_models_combined Applies per ACCOUNT.

xkiro.evidence: The largest confirmed free token allowance in this list by a wide margin, and it took one GET to find - it was sitting behind an endpoint nobody had asked. Requests per day are NOT published; the ceiling here is tokens. 5,000,000 tokens/day is the provider's own token figure (MEASURED). Binding limit: Tokens, not requests. 5M/day is roughly 3,500 pages of output, so on this provider you will hit model quality or latency long before you hit the quota. Applies per ACCOUNT.

burst.what: 30-second burst, per provider, latest reading; bench/throughput.py; a rate, never a day

ceilings_per_minute.note: Output-only and combined in+out ceilings are two shelves and are never added together; only the output-only shelf is compared with the output target.

grants.quote: Each model (such as qwen-plus, qwen3.6-plus, or qwen3.6-plus-2026-04-02) has its own independent free quota (typically 1,000,000 tokens). Quota cannot be merged or transferred across models.

one_time.note: true exactly once; never added to the daily shelf. A grant recorded per_model is per model, not multiplied by the models this list tracks.

grants.quote: Free accounts include a starter amount of usage for a smaller set of starter models. Instead, your included amount refreshes at each monthly reset.

drawn.note: not counted: the only free capacity here is a one-time grant of 4,000,000 tokens, and at the drawn rate it lasts about 6 hours; a grant is not a day
not on the shelf: a DERIVED daily figure already exists

note: defensible_tokens_per_day = MEASURED + DECLARED + DERIVED + DRAWN, largest figure per provider, and it is the only number the bar and the distance use. PAID-PLAN is shown and never counted. Bursts and ceilings are per minute and are never multiplied out to a day. Money is never converted into tokens.
